newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz denies Credit Lyonnais bid report.
newsitem.headline: Allianz denies Credit Lyonnais bid report.

text.p: Allianz AG Holding, Europe's leading insurer, on Wednesday denied a published report that it was interested in taking over the troubled French state-owned bank, Credit Lyonnais.

An Allianz spokesman said the French takeover was "not an issue" for the giant Munich-based insurance group, which is frequently mentioned as a possible buyer for banks and insurers throughout Europe.

Germany's Wirtschaftswoche magazine had reported that Allianz chairman Henning Schulte-Noelle had offered to buy 10 percent of Credit Lyonnais from the French government, with an option for a full takeover at some point in the future.
The magazine said the price would be a symbolic one French franc, on the basis that Credit Lyonnais's valuation would be adjusted to account for its heavy debts.
Credit Lyonnais, regarded as the biggest disaster in the French banking sector, is expected to receive a substantial government bail-out, the third in its history, to ready it for privatisation.
Allianz is known to be keen to expand its presence in France, which it regards as a key market. The German group already co-operates with Credit Lyonnais in the region.
